AC amendment (gap-analysis, missing_error_path; TEMPERED to honor dd-2's {pass,fail,skip} vocabulary): timeout (124) and interrupted (130) still map to 'fail' (dd-2 mandates the canonical 3-token vocabulary — a 4th 'infra_error' token would violate dd-2). BUT the test MUST emit a DISTINGUISHING diagnostic line (e.g. 'INFRA: <engine> on <case> timed out (124)' / 'interrupted (130)') so an infra timeout is identifiable in output and not silently conflated with a substantive assertion failure. Note for downstream 8d15 (parallelism increases timeout likelihood): 8d15 should revisit whether timeouts need separate handling once parallel execution lands.
  Verify: bash -c 'source tests/runners/test-runner-equivalence.sh; [ "$(normalize_verdict suite_engine "" 124)" = fail ]' && grep -Eqi 'INFRA|timed out|timeout|interrupted' tests/runners/test-runner-equivalence.sh
